purpose: Record five more lower-scoring cross-window candidates checked against complete question text, options, answer keys and explanations.

preserved.subject: Physics
preserved.question_a: Specific heat capacity is the energy required to raise the temperature of unit mass of a substance by:
preserved.question_b: The heat required to change a substance from liquid to gas at constant temperature is its latent heat of ___.
preserved.reason: Specific heat capacity measures energy per unit mass per degree of temperature rise; latent heat of vaporisation concerns a phase change at constant temperature. They are different quantities and processes.

preserved.subject: Use of English
preserved.question_a: Which of the following is a complex sentence?
preserved.question_b: Which sentence is in the passive voice?
preserved.reason: The first tests complex sentence structure (main plus subordinate clause); the second tests passive voice construction. A sentence may exhibit both properties, but the questions assess different grammatical features.

preserved.subject: Biology
preserved.question_a: Which chamber of the human heart pumps oxygenated blood into the aorta?
preserved.question_b: Which blood vessel carries deoxygenated blood from the heart to the lungs?
preserved.reason: The first identifies the chamber that pumps oxygenated blood into systemic circulation; the second identifies the vessel carrying deoxygenated blood to the lungs. Different structures and directions of flow.

preserved.subject: Government
preserved.question_a: A successful motion of no confidence in a parliamentary system usually indicates that:
preserved.answer_a: A — the government has lost the confidence of the legislature
preserved.question_b: In a parliamentary system, the cabinet is usually composed mainly of
preserved.answer_b: A — senior ministers who direct major areas of government policy
preserved.reason: A no-confidence motion concerns legislative support and government tenure; cabinet composition concerns the membership and role of the executive's senior ministers. Related parliamentary institutions, but different learning outcomes.

preserved.subject: Economics
preserved.question_a: The balance of payments records a country's:
preserved.answer_a: A — transactions with the rest of the world
preserved.question_b: A country's balance of trade in goods is the difference between the value of its
preserved.answer_b: B — exports and imports of goods
preserved.reason: The balance of payments is the broader record of transactions between residents and the rest of the world; the balance of trade in goods is one component comparing goods exports and imports. The broader account and its narrower component are not duplicates.

controls.note: All five candidates were preserved as distinct after full-content comparison. Similarity alone did not justify any duplicate classification.
